champion: Infiltrative ductal carcinoma of the breast
ordered_diagnoses: Infiltrative ductal carcinoma of the breast
Breast cancer with axillary lymph node metastasis

facts.raw_span: A 48-year-old woman
type 2 diabetes
hypertension
bilateral breast lumps of one-week duration
no family history of breast or ovarian cancer
a 4 × 4 cm hard lump in the lower inner quadrant fixed to the chest wall
MRI showed a 3.8 × 3.5 cm irregular spiculated mass in the left breast suspicious for malignancy
a 2.3 × 1.5 cm well-defined lesion in the right breast with a type 1 contrast enhancement pattern (< 6% probability of malignancy)
bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy
poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and prominent nucleoli
infiltrative duct cell carcinoma that was estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive
FNAC of the left axillary lymph node showed similar malignant cells

concepts.preferred_label: Infiltrative ductal carcinoma of the breast
concepts.why: The patient has a hard lump in the left breast fixed to the chest wall, MRI shows a spiculated mass suspicious for malignancy, and FNAC and core-needle biopsy confirm infiltrative ductal carcinoma.
The patient has a firm, mobile lump in the right breast and MRI shows a well-defined lesion with a low probability of malignancy, consistent with a fibroadenoma.

concepts.preferred_label: Breast cancer with axillary lymph node metastasis
concepts.why: The patient has bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy and FNAC of the left axillary lymph node shows malignant cells, indicating metastasis.

rationales.F06: The presence of a hard lump fixed to the chest wall is highly suggestive of malignancy.
rationales.F07: The MRI findings of an irregular spiculated mass are highly suspicious for malignancy.
rationales.F10: The cytology results showing poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism and hyperchromasia are diagnostic of carcinoma.
rationales.F11: The presence of estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive infiltrative duct cell carcinoma is diagnostic of breast cancer.
rationales.F12: The presence of similar malignant cells in the axillary lymph node is diagnostic of metastasis.

frontier_selector.champion: Infiltrative ductal carcinoma of the breast
frontier_selector.runner_up: Breast cancer with axillary lymph node metastasis
frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's left breast lump was confirmed to be infiltrative duct cell carcinoma with estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive, and FNAC of the left axillary lymph node showed similar malignant cells, supporting the diagnosis of breast cancer with axillary lymph node metastasis, but the most specific diagnosis is infiltrative ductal carcinoma of the breast.
